newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close slightly lower.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange closed slightly lower Friday in weak trade as the market continued to nervously watch developments in the labor sector and foreign exchange markets, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share .IBC index slipped 0.32 percent to 9,435.48, as 23 stocks rose, 18 fell and six closed unchanged.
The failure of business and union leaders to reach an agreement to avert an Aug 6 12-hour national work stoppage contributed to an already muted session, brokers said.
"Large investors are waiting to see what happens about the strikes and wage rises," said Interacciones broker Piero Montelli.
Montelli added that recent turbulence on currency markets, where the bolivar has depreciated by two percent in the last month, had contributed to nervousness.
But the market's uncertainty, would not last long, he said. "It's a temporary situation...afterwards the market will take off."
A total of 1,130 trades for 6,549 billion bolivars ($13.2 million) took place.

Among leading stocks, benchmark Electricidad de Caracas rose 7.00 bolivars to 818.00 bolivars, telephone company CANTV fell 47.00 bolivars to 3,043.00 bolivars and steel company Sivensa slipped 3.00 bolivars to 275.00 bolivars.
Brokers noted heavy trading in holding company H.L. Boulton and CO SACA which rose 5.50 bolivars to 46.00 bolivars after posting sharply improved earnings for the financial year to June 30.
